# D365 CE Roster

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-readme.py. Edit that script, not this file. -->

**Your Dynamics 365 CRM project team as installable AI agents: roles, skills and tailored templates for Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service, from SMB to enterprise.**

D365 CE Roster models the team you need to deliver a Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement (CRM) project as an agent organisation: 17 departments and 100 skills, each department installable on its own. It runs in Claude Code, ChatGPT, Codex and Microsoft Copilot Cowork from the same files. Ask a question in a department's territory and the right specialist loads. Describe your organisation once and the project-tailoring department fills your project roles from your team's declared skills, shows the gaps, and produces the templates and documents your project needs.

> **Status: first draft.** All 100 skills are drafts (100 draft, 0 reviewed). Robert Peledie is reviewing them department by department; see the [roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md).

Project homepage: https://simonfoote-greensparx.github.io/dynamics-365-ce-roster/ (once GitHub Pages is enabled).

## Install

**Claude Code.** Add the marketplace once, then install the departments your project needs:

```
/plugin marketplace add SimonFoote-greensparx/dynamics-365-ce-roster
/plugin install customer-service@dynamics-365-ce-roster
/plugin install solution-architecture@dynamics-365-ce-roster
/plugin install design-authority@dynamics-365-ce-roster
```

**ChatGPT and Codex.** The same repository. Add it as a plugin marketplace (the manifest is `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`), or copy the department folders you want into `.agents/skills/` in your project. Skill descriptions share a limited context budget there, so install a few departments rather than all of them.

**Microsoft Copilot Cowork.** Each department is packaged as a plugin archive in [`cowork/plugins/`](cowork/plugins/). Download the ones you need, then in Cowork select **Customize** > **Plugins** > **Upload plugin**; Cowork converts each archive into a plugin with its skills. [docs/COPILOT-COWORK.md](docs/COPILOT-COWORK.md) covers single skills, suggested custom instructions, tailored project packs in OneDrive, and sharing with your team.

Start with the modules you are implementing, plus `solution-architecture`, `programme-management` and the two reviewer departments. [docs/GETTING-STARTED.md](docs/GETTING-STARTED.md) has a starter set for each kind of project.

## Use

Skills load themselves when a request matches. Ask in plain language:

| You ask | What loads |
|---|---|
| "How should we route chats and emails to the right agents?" | `customer-service:queues-and-routing` |
| "Should we build this as a plug-in or a flow?" | `solution-architecture:extend-or-configure` |
| "Can we email these trade contacts without consent?" | `security-compliance:marketing-consent-compliance` |
| "Here is our team and estate; who should do what?" | `project-tailoring:role-mapping` |

Or name a skill when you want a specific lens: `/field-service:scheduling-optimisation` in Claude Code, or "use the scheduling optimisation skill" elsewhere. Skills are addressed as `department:skill`, so names never collide.

## Tailored project packs

Describe your organisation once in a YAML profile: its team (with declared skills and availability), goals, modules and users, and current estate. Start from a fictional sample in [`profiles/samples/`](profiles/samples/), save your own copy in [`input/`](input/) (git-ignored, so it never reaches the repository), then ask the agent to build your pack. You get:

- the recommended edition (SMB or Enterprise) and why;
- your project roles filled with named people or aliases, with a reason for each match, and unsafe role combinations flagged;
- the uncovered roles, with a recommendation of training, contractor or partner for each;
- 12 ready-to-complete Word and Excel documents, written to `output/` (also git-ignored).

Role mapping uses only the skills and availability people declare. It never ranks people or assesses performance, and its output is a proposal for the project lead to confirm.

| Template | Format | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| [Cutover and hypercare checklist](templates/cutover-and-hypercare-checklist.md) | xlsx | `support-operations:cutover-plan` |
| [Data migration mapping workbook](templates/data-migration-mapping.md) | xlsx | `integration-and-data:data-mapping-and-cleansing` |
| [Delivery plan and milestones](templates/delivery-plan.md) | xlsx | `programme-management:delivery-plan` |
| [Environment and ALM strategy](templates/environment-and-alm-strategy.md) | docx | `solution-architecture:environment-strategy` |
| [Integration inventory](templates/integration-inventory.md) | xlsx | `integration-and-data:integration-architecture` |
| [Project charter and business case](templates/project-charter.md) | docx | `programme-management:project-charter` |
| [Roles and responsibilities (RACI)](templates/raci-matrix.md) | xlsx | `project-tailoring:role-mapping` |
| [RAID log](templates/raid-log.md) | xlsx | `programme-management:raid-log` |
| [Resource and skills-gap plan](templates/resource-and-skills-gap-plan.md) | xlsx | `project-tailoring:skills-gap-analysis` |
| [Solution blueprint outline](templates/solution-blueprint.md) | docx | `solution-architecture:solution-blueprint` |

| [Training and communications plan](templates/training-and-communications-plan.md) | docx | `change-adoption:role-based-training` |

## Scale: SMB and Enterprise editions

Every skill carries SMB and Enterprise notes. The same core skills can also be emitted as two editions with `python3 scripts/build-edition.py --all`, which splices edition-specific context from [`editions/`](editions/) into each skill. SMB assumes one or two apps, a small partner-led team and mostly standard configuration; Enterprise assumes several modules in parallel, a workstream per module, a design authority and formal SIT and UAT.

## Sources

Skills answer from practitioner judgement and point to the authority that settles the question: 31 sources so far, from Microsoft Learn and Microsoft's licensing resources to the ICO and W3C. References, never copies; each entry records what you may do with it. See [docs/SOURCES.md](docs/SOURCES.md).

## Repository layout

```
plugins/<department>/            one installable department
  .claude-plugin/plugin.json     manifest for Claude Code (generated)
  .codex-plugin/plugin.json      manifest for ChatGPT and Codex (generated)
  skills/<skill>/SKILL.md        the skill; frontmatter name equals the folder name
  skills/<skill>/references/     the skill's sources (generated)
catalogue/departments.toml       single source of truth for department metadata
data/                            role catalogue, role combinations, skills vocabulary
profiles/                        organisation profile schema and fictional samples
templates/                       the project templates the tailoring department fills
editions/                        SMB and Enterprise context fragments
sources/                         the source catalogue
tests/triggers/                  trigger tests for every skill
cowork/                          plugin archives and custom instructions for Microsoft Copilot Cowork
input/  output/                  your own profiles and generated packs (git-ignored)
.claude/agents/                  one agent charter per department
docs/                            documentation and the project website (GitHub Pages)
scripts/                         generators and checks; check-all.sh runs everything CI runs
```

## Contributing

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), then run every check locally:

```
bash scripts/check-all.sh
```

Generated files (this README, the manifests, department READMEs, per-skill sources and the website catalogue) are never edited by hand. Change the source and regenerate with `bash scripts/build-all.sh`.
